note: X reverses the sense in 'οἱ δὲ μαχομένοις ἑαυτοῖς δὲ συνίσασι' (print: 'ὃ'=οὐ συνίσασι), also 'καὶ ὃ σαφῶς', 'περιέψεσθαι' for 'περιστῆναι', 'σύνοικον' for 'σύσοιχον' and 'εἴτε' for 'οὔτε'; Y has smaller slips ('ἃ τοιαῦτα', 'ἢ πατᾶσθαι', 'ἐφεχελίας').
The two are nearly equivalent; Y keeps the printed 'γένους τε τῶν' and 'quo tempore & Xenocrates', where X drops the '&'.
The texts are identical apart from X's accent typo 'ἀμφότεραὶ' and how the 'ARIST. RHET. A' footer is tagged.
X has the typos 'euaferant', 'superfstructa' and 'medacius', where Y gives 'euaserant', 'superstructā' and 'mēdacius' as printed; the Greek table of contents is the same in both.
The wording is the same; they differ only in markup (<term>, subscripts, column-break in the footnote).
The texts are the same except for punctuation spacing ('ἂν ·' vs 'ἄν·') and the quote mark form.
X has 'θάλασσαν' where the page prints 'θάλατταν', and in the apparatus 'τὰ] ἴσα FM' where the page has 'ὅσα FM'; Y matches the page in both places.

X misreads the hand throughout ('ὡρισμένους … σεκουνιακοὺς' for 'ὠριγενιαστὰς … κοινωνικοὺς', invents 'παρὰ τὸ πρόσωπον ἠκρωτηρίασε', and gives 'Ἰωάννου ἄξιον' for 'τοῦ ἁγίου'), while Y follows it closely; Y does misnumber the charges as 'ια, ιβ, ιγ' where the page has ιε, ιϛ, ιζ.
X adds 'ὁ πρῶτος ἄρτος' and has 'τά σφι ἔπεσσε' and 'καὶ ἐκάλεσε', where the manuscript reads 'ὁ ἄρτος', 'τὰ σιτία ἔπεσσε' and 'καλέσας δὲ'; Y follows the manuscript more closely.
The wording is the same; X puts the lemma 'utpote quae…' in a blockquote, while Y bolds it inline as the page prints it.
